notes.expected_mcu: The die proves family and flash size, not package or temperature grade. identify.py asserts DBGMCU IDCODE DEV_ID == 0x468 and FLASH_SIZE == 128 KiB and reports STM32G431xB. The KBU6 suffix (UFQFPN32) is corroborated by the board itself: PF0 carries TIM1_CH3N, and PF0 is only bonded out on the 32-pin package.
notes.expected_probe_serial: ST-LINK/V2, USB 0483:3748, read from /sys/bus/usb/devices/3-4/serial. The descriptor holds a raw 12-byte serial; the adapters convert it to the canonical 24-hex-digit form. OpenOCD's own serial filter is not used, because that binary string cannot be passed through an argv safely -- instead the adapters refuse to run unless exactly one ST-LINK is attached and its serial matches this value.
notes.flash_range: STM32G431KB: 128 KiB main flash at 0x08000000..0x08020000. There is no bootloader reservation in this project; the application links at 0x08000000, so the ELF entry point must lie in this range.
notes.flash_leaves_target_halted: flash.py clears TIM1 MOE, programs with verify, then issues `reset halt` and reads BDTR/CCER/CR1 back. It never resumes. hilctl checks this independently with verify_halted.py before any bounded test.
notes.firmware_starts_disarmed: Enforced by construction in the firmware and re-checked on every trial: run_trial.py resumes the target, waits for hil_state, and fails the trial with signature `firmware-not-disarmed` if state != STOP or TIM1 MOE is set before the arm key is written.
notes.stop_path: stop.py halts, clears TIM1 MOE (this is what releases the six MP6540HA gate inputs), zeroes CCER and CR1, then `reset halt`, then reads the registers back and exits nonzero unless the off-state is confirmed. Halting the core alone is not a stop -- TIM1 keeps running and keeps commutating while the CPU is stopped.
notes.capture: Not configured as a separate hilctl step. tools/hil-adapters/run_trial.py writes the full trial trace to .hil/logs/<trial_id>/test-evidence.json and the on-chip gate capture to gate-capture.bin itself, which keeps a fatal extra step out of the loop. The adapter is named run_trial.py rather than test.py so that importing it can never pick up Python's stdlib `test` package.
